messages.content: I want to go to whistler for skiing. Can you give me the 5 day forecast for both the top and bottom of the mountain.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data. This function is commonly used for API calls and web scraping. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.reasoning:
The user wants a 5-day weather forecast for Whistler ski area, specifically for top and bottom of the mountain. We need to provide forecast info.

We don't have direct weather APIs integrated; we could call an external API like open-meteo.com or WeatherAPI. But no tool defined except requests_get. So we can make a GET request to some public API providing forecasts. For example, open-meteo has free endpoints: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=... etc. That returns JSON with daily temperature, precipitation probability, wind speed, etc. However it doesn't differentiate between top/bottom of mountain. Could approximate using elevation differences: top ~1700m vs base ~1200m maybe. Some APIs allow specifying elevation but many do not. Alternatively we might fetch two separate coordinates representing top and bottom positions. Use lat/lon for top (~50.1167°N, -122.9578°W?) Actually Whistler Village at approx 50.1139,-121.9700. Top of Blackcomb Mountain around 51.0?? Wait let's check approximate coordinates:

Whistler Ski Resort includes several peaks: Blackcomb peak at about 52.000? Let's quickly recall: Whistler Blackcomb summit altitude 2000 m above sea level. Coordinates roughly 49.99°N, -123.02°W? Might be near 50.12°, -121.97°. We'll just pick approximate coordinates: Base station at 50.112, -121.971. Summit at 50.13, -121.95? Not accurate. Maybe better to get actual coordinates via quick knowledge: According to Wikipedia, Whistler village latitude 50.114°, longitude -121.969°. Blackcomb Peak coordinate 50.133°N, -121.950°W. That's close enough.

Thus we can produce forecast for those two points separately. Provide 5 days forecast: high/low temps, snowfall chance, wind speeds, cloud cover, etc.

We'll use open-meteo endpoint: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,windspeed_10m_max,snowfall_sum,precipitation_probability_mean&timezone=AEST? Actually timezone should match local zone: Pacific Time (America/Vancouver). Use &hourly? No only daily needed.

But open-meteo also supports elevation param? I think they support "elevation" optional param. Yes there is "elevation" param. So we can set different elevations: e.g., base 1200m, summit 1900m. Then same location but diff elevation yields slightly different forecast. Good idea! So we can keep same lat lon but specify elevation difference.

Open-Meteo docs: Parameter "elevation": integer meters. Default 0. Accepts up to 5000. Great.

So we can call once for each elevation: base 1200, summit 1900. Or we can combine into one request? They accept multiple queries? Probably easier to call twice.

Let's craft URLs:
Base: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=50.115&longitude=-121.972&elevation=1200&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,windspeed_10m_max,snowfall_sum,precipitation_probability_mean&timeformat=iso8601&timezone=PST

Summit: same lat lon but elevation=1900.

Then parse JSON and present table.

Need to handle potential errors. Also note that open-meteo uses UTC times; timezone PST ensures correct dates.

Will call function requests_get accordingly.

Also mention limitations: forecast based on models, not guaranteed.

Ok proceed.
